findings.issue_text: String#scrub does not exist on Ruby 2.0 targeted by this codebase, causing NoMethodError that kills the hourly poll job every run and breaks feed importing entirely
Job assumes every feed item exposes :content; RSS 2.0 items with only <description> yield nil, and nil.scrub raises NoMethodError aborting the whole poll including items that do have content

New gems ruby-readability and simple-rss added to Gemfile but primary Gemfile.lock not updated (only Gemfile_rails4.lock regenerated), causing bundler failures in frozen/deployment mode or LoadError at runtime

New top-level 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js assets are referenced but no config.assets.precompile entry is added, so embed.css is never precompiled in production causing Sprockets errors/500s and /assets/embed.js 404s
Migration defaults cook_method to 1 (raw_html), making all existing posts skip cooking/sanitization and render raw markdown/HTML verbatim
Imported feed HTML is never sanitized: PollFeed stores CGI.unescapeHTML content with raw_html cook_method and best.html.erb renders raw post.cooked, allowing script injection
Import failure has no error state: fetch_http, TopicRetriever.retrieve, and import silently fail, causing client to reload every 30 seconds forever showing 'Loading Discussion...'
embed_url is never canonicalized while topic_id_for_embed requires exact string equality, causing duplicate topics or permanent loading due to trailing slash/http/https/utm/www differences
absolutize_urls only handles leading-slash URLs: relative URLs like 'images/wat.jpg' stay broken and protocol-relative URLs like '//cdn.example/x.png' are mangled with a duplicated slash

PollFeed has no handling for feed items without content (raises NoMethodError for Atom entries with only summary) and no per-item error isolation, so one bad item aborts the rest of the poll with retry: false
EmbedController requires the Referer header to match embeddable_host with no fallback, breaking embeds for visitors whose browsers/extensions strip Referer
TopicEmbed.import has a check-then-create race against the unique index: no rescue of RecordNotUnique when concurrent jobs import the same URL
feed_key is defined but never called; the conditional-poll caching optimization was never wired up so the feed is fully re-fetched every hour
embed.js has no guard for a missing #discourse-comments element and no trailing-slash normalization of discourseUrl, producing thrown errors or malformed iframe src like 'forum.comembed/best'
Scope drift: PR title promises 'enhanced embed URL handling and validation' but the diff delivers an entire new RSS comment embedding subsystem with no traceability to the stated requirement

Critical sanitization gap: PollFeed feeds raw CGI.unescapeHTML'd third-party feed markup into TopicEmbed.import with cook_method: :raw_html, which makes Post#cook skip the entire cooking/sanitization pipeline, and the view renders it with raw post.cooked — enabling stored XSS from untrusted RSS content
Unrelated regression: lib/tasks/disqus.thor removes the --category option and all category_id handling, breaking existing disqus:import CLI invocations and silently losing category assignment
Unrelated migration edit adds force: true to the already-shipped create_top_topics migration, which will silently drop and recreate the table on rebuilds, destroying computed topic statistics

feed_key in PollFeed is dead code: the Redis key is computed but never read or written, so the intended per-feed change-detection was never implemented and every feed item is re-imported on every hourly run
No failure state for embed retrieval: the loading page reloads every 30 seconds unconditionally, so if import fails the iframe reloads forever with no error or terminal state

Origin check in embed.js is a substring match (indexOf) instead of equality, allowing attacker origins like https://forum.example.com.evil.io to forge discourse-resize messages and manipulate iframe height
Admin menu entry 'Embedding' added to client.en.yml with no backing admin route, controller, or JS template — dead UI string shipped without implementation
Whitespace-only drive-by edits to the unrelated migrate_word_counts migration, inflating review surface and risking merge conflicts

topic_embed.rb import assigns untrusted external HTML the trusted cook path (cook_method: :raw_html), bypassing the entire rendering pipeline including after_post_cook sanitization filters, and raw post.cooked is rendered unescaped in embed/best.html.erb
EmbedController enqueues a retrieve_topic job on every /embed/best request with no throttle before enqueue, flooding Sidekiq with duplicate no-op jobs for popular pages
Embed failure path has no terminal state: loading.html.erb reloads every 30s forever, re-enqueueing jobs indefinitely with no backoff, cap, or give-up state
poll_feed.rb raises NoMethodError on Atom entries without a content element, and with retry: false and no per-item rescue, one poison item permanently blocks import of all subsequent feed items
poll_feed.rb's rss.items.each loop is unbounded: first run against a large archive imports every item in a single job

TopicRetriever synchronously executes the scheduled PollFeed job inline (Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute) within a user-triggered RetrieveTopic job, running full network fetch and import on the request path with no coordination between the two scheduling owners
topic_embeds migration has no FK, no index on topic_id/post_id, and no cleanup on topic deletion, so orphaned embeds render errors forever instead of triggering re-import
TopicEmbed identity is raw URL string equality with no normalization, so near-duplicate URLs (http vs https, trailing slash, utm params) create duplicate topics for the same article

embeddable_host and feed_polling_url are scalar site settings, so the data model supports only one embeddable site and one feed; adding a second blog requires overwriting the setting and breaks the first site's embeds
EmbedController authenticates by Referer header comparison, which hard-fails 404 for legitimate visitors whose browsers or extensions strip the Referer header

poll_feed.rb defines feed_key ('feed-modified:...') but never reads or writes it — the implied conditional polling/Last-Modified caching strategy doesn't exist, so every hourly run re-parses the full feed

Post#cook's 'return raw' path for raw_html bypasses the Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...) contract, silently no-oping plugins (sanitizers, link rewriting) for imported posts via a hidden second cooking path

TopicRetriever has a TOCTOU race on duplicate import: the exists? check then import_remote allows concurrent retrieves; the unique index catches the insert but the failure relies on TopicEmbed.create! raising an unhandled exception rather than handling the race

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117 (and 140-145): Existing disqus import tool's contract silently rewritten in unrelated feature PR — deleting the :category option breaks existing scripts/automation invoking 'disqus import -c', with no migration path

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117 (and 140-145): Import semantics silently flipped from creating a permalink-stub topic (deterministic, no network I/O) to fetching and parsing live remote articles, causing failures/hangs on dead or moved links and raw-HTML-cooked output instead of link stubs, contradicting the PR title 'Enhance embed URL handling and validation'

db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:5: Adding force: true to an already-shipped historical migration makes any rollback-and-re-run destructively drop and recreate top_topics, destroying computed topic statistics, and causes upgraded and fresh installs to run different effective schema history
db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:5: Editing an applied migration appears to be a patch-over of a 'table already exists' development failure without addressing the root cause

app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33 + app/models/post.rb:131-134 + app/views/embed/best.html.erb:21: raw_html cook path silently deletes the 'cooked content is always sanitized' invariant — poll_feed passes unsanitized feed HTML through TopicEmbed.import to PostCreator with cook_method raw_html, which skips the sanitization pipeline, and best.html.erb renders it with raw, allowing persisted and executed HTML/JS in the forum origin and in every third-party embedding page via embed.js
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33: The ruby-readability tag whitelist used in TopicEmbed.import_remote is not exercised by PollFeed, which passes i.content straight to import with zero filtering

app/models/topic_embed.rb:20: 'Imported from' attribution link interpolates an unvalidated, attacker-controllable URL (from feed item link/id or embed_url request parameter) directly into a single-quoted href HTML attribute, enabling attribute breakout and HTML/JS injection into post bodies — contradicting the PR's stated objective of embed URL validation

Stored XSS: untrusted third-party RSS feed HTML rendered unescaped via `raw post.cooked` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:23; the raw_html cook method (post.rb:132-134) short-circuits the cooking/sanitize pipeline, so <script>, <iframe>, onerror= handlers, and javascript: hrefs from the polled feed are stored verbatim and served to every viewer of the embed and topic pages

Attribute-injection XSS in app/models/topic_embed.rb:12: user-supplied embed_url is interpolated unescaped into an HTML attribute (#{url}); validation only checks for http(s) prefix and host equality, so a URL containing a single quote or >"> payload injects arbitrary attributes/elements that become stored XSS

SSRF via redirect in TopicEmbed.import_remote + TopicRetriever: server-side open(url).read follows HTTP redirects without re-validating the host, and the DNS-rebinding gap (separate DNS resolutions between host check and connection) allows bouncing the fetch to internal addresses such as http://169.254.169.254/, cloud metadata endpoints, or internal admin panels, with fetched content persisted into public topics

Trust-the-client authorization in app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26: the Referer header is the sole authorization gate and is client-controlled/trivially forged, so any anonymous user can fetch embed/best for any URL and enqueue arbitrary retrieve_topic background jobs causing the server to fetch attacker-chosen URLs; the 30s auto-reloading loading view amplifies load

Unsafe postMessage target in app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:10: attacker-controlled request.referer is interpolated into an inline <script> string context; currently protected only by incidental ERB HTML-escaping behavior, and any escaping change or html_safe use would enable direct script injection; posting to the full referer URL also leaks the parent page's path and query to the iframe target

Fragile origin check in embed.js:17: discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 is a substring match rather than origin equality (indexOf(...) === 0), so a parent at https://evil-host.example.com would be accepted if discourseUrl contains it as a substring
embed.js:17 assigns e.data.height to iframe height without validating it is a number, allowing malformed style values (limited impact, no injection sink beyond the height attribute)
app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:36 calls i.content.scrub which raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content element, a reliability bug
PollFeed#feed_key computes a cache key that is never used, so the feed is re-fetched and re-imported hourly with only the SHA1 dedupe protecting against churn

Guard tests in spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:16-26 for 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' pass for the wrong reason: the stubbed settings are never evaluated because Ruby's && short-circuits on the default-false feed_polling_enabled, so deleting SiteSetting.feed_polling_url.present? or SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present? from the guard would still keep tests green

The entire body of poll_feed in app/jobs/poll_feed.rb:26-40 has zero test coverage; RSS parsing, Atom fallback URL fix, CGI.unescapeHTML on possibly-nil content (NoMethodError risk), and the TopicEmbed.import loop are never executed — only mock-invocation of the private method is verified

The 'valid host' tests in spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:31-43 stub retrieved_recently?, mirroring the implementation against itself; the real Redis throttle logic ($redis.setnx / $redis.expire at lib/topic_retriever.rb:24-30) and the staff no_throttle bypass in app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:20 are never exercised

perform_retrieve's real decision logic is stubbed in every test in spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, leaving the 'bail if embed already exists' check, the RSS-first branch, fetch_http fall-through, and the 'return if user.blank?' guard untested; the new app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb job (InvalidParameters raise, staff no_throttle derivation) also has no spec

The skip-validations branch at lib/post_revisor.rb:85 is only exercised with data that passes validation anyway (spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:40-43 revises with a valid body), so the behavioral change of save(validate: false) is never verified; a test revising to content that fails validation is needed

The update-path test in spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:40-43 never asserts that the new content_sha1 was persisted via update_column, so deleting that line would still keep the test green while causing repeated revise-branch re-entry on every feed poll

The 'creates a topic view when a topic_id is found' test in spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:49-53 stubs TopicView.new with a mock, so only the constructor call is verified; bad 'best: 5' options, TopicView argument-contract changes, and rendering regressions against real data would go undetected

add_column :posts, :cook_method with DEFAULT + NOT NULL causes full table rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on PostgreSQL <11, blocking all reads/writes on posts during deploy; safe pattern (add nullable → backfill → set NOT NULL) not used

topic_embeds rows have NOT NULL topic_id/post_id but no foreign keys and no dependent: cleanup, so deleting a topic/post leaves orphaned rows that cause EmbedController#best to 500 and TopicRetriever/PollFeed to raise NoMethodError with no purge step

embed_url is a varchar(255) with unique index but URLs longer than 255 chars are valid; PollFeed has no per-item rescue and retry: false, so an over-length URL raises StatementInvalid, aborts the entire feed poll run, permanently blocks all subsequent items in that feed, and data loss goes unreported

Already-shipped migration create_top_topics is edited to add force: true, which will silently DROP and recreate a populated top_topics table on databases where the table exists but the version row is missing (e.g., restored backup), losing all topic ranking data

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: String#scrub does not exist on Ruby 2.0 targeted by this codebase, causing NoMethodError that kills the hourly poll job every run and breaks feed importing entirely

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the code does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. `String#scrub` is not available in Ruby 2.0 (it was introduced later), so on a Ruby 2.0 runtime this line will raise `NoMethodError`, causing the scheduled poll job to fail whenever it runs and preventing feed imports. The diff does not add any compatibility shim for `scrub`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Job assumes every feed item exposes :content; RSS 2.0 items with only <description> yield nil, and nil.scrub raises NoMethodError aborting the whole poll including items that do have content
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same underlying bug: the code assumes every RSS item has `content`, so when `content` is nil (common when only `<description>` is provided), calling `.scrub` causes a NoMethodError and can crash the poll. This aligns with the golden issue about needing a fallback (e.g., to `description`) to avoid nil exceptions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New gems ruby-readability and simple-rss added to Gemfile but primary Gemfile.lock not updated (only Gemfile_rails4.lock regenerated), causing bundler failures in frozen/deployment mode or LoadError at runtime

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` to `Gemfile` and updates `Gemfile_rails4.lock` accordingly. However, the diff does not show a `Gemfile.lock` file at all, so it’s not verifiable from this change that a “primary Gemfile.lock” exists or is expected to be updated. The claim about bundler failures in frozen/deployment mode depends on repository setup outside the diff (which lockfile is actually used).

adjudication_records.issue_text: New top-level 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js assets are referenced but no config.assets.precompile entry is added, so embed.css is never precompiled in production causing Sprockets errors/500s and /assets/embed.js 404s

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new assets (app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss and app/assets/javascripts/embed.js) and references the stylesheet via `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` in the new `embed` layout. However, the diff does not show the app’s asset pipeline configuration (e.g., `config/initializers/assets.rb` or any existing `config.assets.precompile` rules), nor whether `embed.css` is already picked up via a wildcard, manifest inclusion, or runtime compilation settings. Additionally, `embed.js` is not referenced anywhere in the added Rails views/layouts in this diff, so the claim that it will 404 from within the app is not directly supported by the shown changes. Therefore the finding asserts a production precompile failure that cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration defaults cook_method to 1 (raw_html), making all existing posts skip cooking/sanitization and render raw markdown/HTML verbatim

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Post.cook_methods` is defined as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`, and existing Discourse enums (e.g., `Post.types Enum.new(:regular, :moderator_action)`) conventionally map the first symbol to value `1`. The migration `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` therefore defaults posts to `:regular`, not `:raw_html`. The `cook` method only skips the cooking pipeline when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. So the change does not make all existing posts skip cooking/sanitization.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Imported feed HTML is never sanitized: PollFeed stores CGI.unescapeHTML content with raw_html cook_method and best.html.erb renders raw post.cooked, allowing script injection

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `:raw_html` cook method that bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline: `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Feed importing (`Jobs::PollFeed`) takes `i.content` (untrusted HTML from RSS/Atom), runs `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and passes it into `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. The embed view then renders the post body with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, and for `raw_html` posts `post.cooked == post.raw`. There is no sanitization step in this path (the Nokogiri `absolutize_urls` only rewrites URLs), so arbitrary HTML (including `<script>`/event handlers) from the feed can be stored and rendered, enabling script injection (stored XSS).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Import failure has no error state: fetch_http, TopicRetriever.retrieve, and import silently fail, causing client to reload every 30 seconds forever showing 'Loading Discussion...'

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` exists it enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and renders `loading`. The `loading.html.erb` view unconditionally reloads the page every 30 seconds. If retrieval never creates a `TopicEmbed` (e.g., `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` returns early when `embed_by_username` user is missing, `invalid_host?` blocks retrieval, or `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/network/parsing fails without persisting any failure state), subsequent requests will keep finding `topic_id_for_embed` as nil and keep rendering the loading page. There is no persisted error/timeout state or alternate render path, so the UI can remain stuck in an infinite reload loop showing “Loading Discussion...”.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_url is never canonicalized while topic_id_for_embed requires exact string equality, causing duplicate topics or permanent loading due to trailing slash/http/https/utm/www differences

adjudication.rationale: The diff stores and looks up embeds by exact `embed_url` string. `EmbedController#best` calls `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` which does `where(embed_url: embed_url)` (exact match). `TopicEmbed.import` persists `embed_url: url` without any normalization, and `TopicRetriever`/`PollFeed` pass through URLs as-provided (from params/feed items). Therefore, variations like `http` vs `https`, trailing slashes, `utm_*` query params, or `www` differences will not match existing records and can cause duplicate `TopicEmbed` rows/topics and repeated “loading”/re-enqueueing behavior because the lookup keeps returning nil for a non-canonicalized variant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls only handles leading-slash URLs: relative URLs like 'images/wat.jpg' stay broken and protocol-relative URLs like '//cdn.example/x.png' are mangled with a duplicated slash

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, links/images are rewritten only when `href`/`src` starts with `'/'`. Relative paths like `'images/wat.jpg'` (no leading slash) are left unchanged, so they will resolve relative to the Discourse host instead of the source article, causing broken URLs. Additionally, protocol-relative URLs like `'//cdn.example/x.png'` also start with `'/'` and will be rewritten to `"#{prefix}/#{...}"` (e.g., `http://sourcehost/cdn.example/x.png`), which is incorrect. (The finding’s “duplicated slash” phrasing isn’t quite accurate because `sub(/^\/+/, '')` removes extra slashes, but the URL is still mangled.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed has no handling for feed items without content (raises NoMethodError for Atom entries with only summary) and no per-item error isolation, so one bad item aborts the rest of the poll with retry: false

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, each item does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed entry lacks `content` (common for Atom entries that only provide `summary`/`description`), `i.content` will be nil and calling `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError. There is also no per-item rescue around the loop, so a single bad item will raise and abort processing of remaining items for that run. Additionally, the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so the failed execution won’t be retried by Sidekiq (it will just fail that poll run).

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbedController requires the Referer header to match embeddable_host with no fallback, breaking embeds for visitors whose browsers/extensions strip Referer

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is denied unless `URI(request.referer || '').host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. If the browser/extension strips the `Referer` header, `request.referer` is nil, `URI('')` yields a nil host, and the comparison fails, raising `Discourse::InvalidAccess` and breaking the embed. This behavior is explicitly exercised in `embed_controller_spec` (“raises an error with no referer”).

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import has a check-then-create race against the unique index: no rescue of RecordNotUnique when concurrent jobs import the same URL

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, it does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank proceeds to `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)`. The migration adds a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`. With concurrent imports of the same URL (e.g., multiple RetrieveTopic jobs or feed polling overlap), both processes can observe `embed.blank?` and both attempt `create!`; the second will raise an `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (or similar) due to the unique index. There is no locking (e.g., SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) and no rescue/retry/lookup-on-conflict handling, so this is a real correctness/race issue present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key is defined but never called; the conditional-poll caching optimization was never wired up so the feed is fully re-fetched every hour

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is indeed defined and never referenced anywhere in the diff, so it is currently dead code. However, the claim that this represents a “conditional-poll caching optimization” that was “never wired up” is not something the diff actually demonstrates: there is no conditional GET / If-Modified-Since logic or any use of `feed_key` to store/reuse a last-modified value. The job fetching the feed hourly is consistent with its scheduled design, and the unused method does not introduce a functional bug by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js has no guard for a missing #discourse-comments element and no trailing-slash normalization of discourseUrl, producing thrown errors or malformed iframe src like 'forum.comembed/best'

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, `comments` is set via `document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and is used immediately with `comments.appendChild(iframe);` with no null check. If the element is missing on the host page, this will throw a runtime error (`Cannot read properties of null`). The code also concatenates `discourseUrl + "embed/best..."` without ensuring a trailing slash, so if `discourseUrl` is configured without a trailing `/` it will produce a malformed path like `forum.comembed/best` (whether that occurs depends on how `discourseUrl` is set elsewhere).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Scope drift: PR title promises 'enhanced embed URL handling and validation' but the diff delivers an entire new RSS comment embedding subsystem with no traceability to the stated requirement

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces a full embedding + feed importing subsystem (new controller, routes, jobs, models, migrations, assets, settings, gems, specs). However, the finding hinges on a claimed PR title/requirement mismatch (“PR title promises ...”) which is not present anywhere in the provided diff, so the alleged scope drift cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Critical sanitization gap: PollFeed feeds raw CGI.unescapeHTML'd third-party feed markup into TopicEmbed.import with cook_method: :raw_html, which makes Post#cook skip the entire cooking/sanitization pipeline, and the view renders it with raw post.cooked — enabling stored XSS from untrusted RSS content

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an RSS/Atom import path that stores and renders third‑party HTML without sanitization. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, it does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passes that into `TopicEmbed.import(...)`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates the first post with `PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), ..., cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`. In `Post#cook`, when `cook_method == :raw_html` it returns `raw` and explicitly skips the normal cooking/filtering pipeline. The embed view then outputs it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Since the feed content is not sanitized (only `.scrub`, which is not HTML sanitization), malicious markup (e.g., `<script>` or event handlers) from an untrusted feed could be persisted and rendered, constituting a stored XSS vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated regression: lib/tasks/disqus.thor removes the --category option and all category_id handling, breaking existing disqus:import CLI invocations and silently losing category assignment

adjudication.rationale: The diff in lib/tasks/disqus.thor removes `method_option :category` and deletes all logic that maps `options[:category]` to a `category_id` and passes it into `PostCreator`. The import path now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which has no category argument, so there is no longer any way for the CLI to assign an imported thread to a specified category. Existing `disqus:import --category ...` invocations would also break because Thor will treat `--category` as an unknown option.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated migration edit adds force: true to the already-shipped create_top_topics migration, which will silently drop and recreate the table on rebuilds, destroying computed topic statistics

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `CreateTopTopics` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop an existing `top_topics` table before creating it. Because this is an already-existing (previously committed) migration, this introduces a real risk of silent data loss if the migration is ever re-run (e.g., migrate:redo/rollback+re-run) or applied in an environment where the table already exists for any reason; without `force: true` it would have errored instead of dropping data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key in PollFeed is dead code: the Redis key is computed but never read or written, so the intended per-feed change-detection was never implemented and every feed item is re-imported on every hourly run

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined to build a Redis key (`"feed-modified:..."`) but it is never referenced anywhere in the class: `execute` calls `poll_feed`, and `poll_feed` unconditionally does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items.each` calling `TopicEmbed.import(...)`. There is no read/write of `feed_key` and no conditional logic using a stored "last modified" value, so any intended per-feed change detection via Redis is not implemented. The job will process all items on every run (though `TopicEmbed.import` will avoid creating duplicates and only updates when the content SHA changes).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No failure state for embed retrieval: the loading page reloads every 30 seconds unconditionally, so if import fails the iframe reloads forever with no error or terminal state

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` which runs `setTimeout(function(){ document.location.reload(); }, 30000);` unconditionally, with no limit or error handling. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`. If the background retrieval fails, is misconfigured (e.g., `embed_by_username` missing), the remote fetch errors, or the embed is never created, `topic_id_for_embed` will continue to be nil and the iframe will reload forever with no terminal/failure state. This behavior is directly verifiable from the added controller/view logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Origin check in embed.js is a substring match (indexOf) instead of equality, allowing attacker origins like https://forum.example.com.evil.io to forge discourse-resize messages and manipulate iframe height
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same vulnerability: origin validation uses indexOf/substring matching rather than strict equality, allowing malicious lookalike domains (e.g., forum.example.com.evil.io / evil-discourseUrl.com) to pass the check and send forged messages.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin menu entry 'Embedding' added to client.en.yml with no backing admin route, controller, or JS template — dead UI string shipped without implementation

adjudication.rationale: The added `embedding: "Embedding"` string in `config/locales/client.en.yml` is not a standalone “admin menu entry” requiring a new route/controller/template. In Discourse, this label is used to name a Site Settings category. The diff also adds an `embedding:` category in `config/site_settings.yml` with settings (`embeddable_host`, `feed_polling_enabled`, etc.) and corresponding server-side setting descriptions in `config/locales/server.en.yml`. Those settings will appear under the existing admin Site Settings UI, so the string is backed by the new settings category and is not dead/unimplemented UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Whitespace-only drive-by edits to the unrelated migrate_word_counts migration, inflating review surface and risking merge conflicts

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes changes to db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb that are unrelated to the embedding feature and appear to be whitespace-only: a line with trailing spaces after `disable_ddl_transaction!` is normalized, and a missing newline at EOF is added (`\ No newline at end of file`). This increases the diff surface for an otherwise unrelated migration and can increase merge conflict risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb import assigns untrusted external HTML the trusted cook path (cook_method: :raw_html), bypassing the entire rendering pipeline including after_post_cook sanitization filters, and raw post.cooked is rendered unescaped in embed/best.html.erb

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In TopicEmbed.import, the new post is created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents)`. In Post#cook, `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (`post_analyzer.cook`) and the `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` hook. The imported `contents` comes from external sources (RSS via `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` / `i.content` and HTTP via `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)`) and is not sanitized in this diff beyond URL absolutizing and Readability tag/attribute selection. Then `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Since `post.cooked` will be the original `raw` HTML under `:raw_html`, untrusted external HTML can be emitted directly, creating a verifiable XSS/sanitization bypass risk introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbedController enqueues a retrieve_topic job on every /embed/best request with no throttle before enqueue, flooding Sidekiq with duplicate no-op jobs for popular pages

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no TopicEmbed exists (topic_id is nil), it unconditionally calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` on every request before rendering `loading`. There is no pre-enqueue deduplication or throttle in the controller. Although TopicRetriever (invoked by the job) has a Redis-based 60s throttle (`retrieved_recently?`) that can make later executions no-ops, those duplicate jobs are still enqueued and will still be popped/executed by Sidekiq, which can flood the queue for a popular page during the window before the embed is created.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embed failure path has no terminal state: loading.html.erb reloads every 30s forever, re-enqueueing jobs indefinitely with no backoff, cap, or give-up state

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no TopicEmbed exists it unconditionally enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) and renders loading. The loading view (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb) always reloads the page after 30s. If the embed never becomes available (e.g., retrieval fails, misconfiguration, bad URL), each reload will hit #best again and enqueue another retrieve_topic job, with no cap/backoff/terminal error state in the diff. Although TopicRetriever has a 60s throttle for the *retrieve* action, that does not prevent the controller from repeatedly enqueuing jobs, so the “failure path loops forever and re-enqueues indefinitely” is a real issue visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb raises NoMethodError on Atom entries without a content element, and with retry: false and no per-item rescue, one poison item permanently blocks import of all subsequent feed items

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. If a feed item lacks a `content` field (common for some Atom/RSS entries, which may only have `description`/`summary`), then `i.content` will be `nil` and `nil.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`. There is no per-item rescue, so a single such item aborts the whole job before processing later items. Additionally, `sidekiq_options retry: false` means the failed run won’t be retried by Sidekiq, and because the scheduled job will hit the same poison item on every run, it can continuously prevent importing subsequent items until the feed/item changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb's rss.items.each loop is unbounded: first run against a large archive imports every item in a single job

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `poll_feed` does `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and then iterates `rss.items.each` with no limit, pagination, or “since last run” filtering. The method `feed_key` (which could be used to track last-modified/etag) is defined but never used. Therefore, on an initial run (or if the feed endpoint returns a large number of items), this single scheduled job will attempt to import every item in one execution, which is a clear unbounded-work/performance defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever synchronously executes the scheduled PollFeed job inline (Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute) within a user-triggered RetrieveTopic job, running full network fetch and import on the request path with no coordination between the two scheduling owners

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` directly calling `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs a network fetch (`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`) and iterates/imports items. `TopicRetriever` is invoked from the user-triggered `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` (enqueued by `EmbedController#best`). This means the scheduled job’s work can be executed synchronously inside another job, bypassing the intended hourly schedule and without any locking/coordination to prevent concurrent/duplicative runs. (It is not literally on the controller request thread, but it is inline in the background job triggered by a request.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embeds migration has no FK, no index on topic_id/post_id, and no cleanup on topic deletion, so orphaned embeds render errors forever instead of triggering re-import

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `topic_embeds` with only a unique index on `embed_url` and no foreign keys or dependent cleanup. `EmbedController#best` trusts `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` and if it returns an id it builds `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)`; if that topic was deleted but the `topic_embeds` row remains, this can raise/404 instead of enqueueing retrieval. Separately, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` bails out early if `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`, so an orphaned/stale `topic_embeds` row will prevent re-import forever. The lack of indexes on `topic_id`/`post_id` is more of a performance concern, but the orphan/stale-row behavior is a real correctness problem visible from the new control flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed identity is raw URL string equality with no normalization, so near-duplicate URLs (http vs https, trailing slash, utm params) create duplicate topics for the same article

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, TopicEmbed identifies an embed solely by exact string equality on `embed_url` (e.g., `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` in `import` and `topic_id_for_embed`). The migration also enforces uniqueness on the raw `embed_url` string (`add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`). There is no URL normalization/canonicalization (scheme, trailing slash, query params, fragments, etc.) before lookup/insert, so semantically equivalent URLs like http vs https or tracking-parameter variants will be treated as distinct and can create separate TopicEmbed rows/topics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embeddable_host and feed_polling_url are scalar site settings, so the data model supports only one embeddable site and one feed; adding a second blog requires overwriting the setting and breaks the first site's embeds

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new site settings as single values (`embeddable_host`, `feed_polling_url`, `embed_by_username`) in `config/site_settings.yml`, and the implementation explicitly uses them as scalars (e.g., `ensure_embeddable` requires `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`; `PollFeed` reads `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`). This does mean the feature, as implemented, only supports one allowed embedding host and one feed URL at a time. However, that is a design choice/limitation rather than a verifiable defect: nothing in the diff indicates the feature is intended to support multiple hosts/feeds, and restricting to a single host is consistent with a security allowlist approach. The finding describes a limitation but not a clear bug/correctness issue introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbedController authenticates by Referer header comparison, which hard-fails 404 for legitimate visitors whose browsers or extensions strip the Referer header

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is gated by comparing `URI(request.referer || '').host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, and it raises `Discourse::InvalidAccess` when they don't match. If the browser/extension strips the `Referer` header, `request.referer` is nil, `URI('')` yields a nil host, and the comparison fails, causing the request to error out even if the embed is otherwise legitimate. (It won’t necessarily be a 404 specifically, but it will hard-fail.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb defines feed_key ('feed-modified:...') but never reads or writes it — the implied conditional polling/Last-Modified caching strategy doesn't exist, so every hourly run re-parses the full feed

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb a `feed_key` method is defined that memoizes a Redis key based on the feed URL (`"feed-modified:..."`), but nothing in this diff ever calls `feed_key` or uses it to read/write any cache/Last-Modified state. The `poll_feed` method always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates items on every run, so the suggested conditional polling/caching mechanism is indeed absent and `feed_key` is dead/unimplemented code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Post#cook's 'return raw' path for raw_html bypasses the Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...) contract, silently no-oping plugins (sanitizers, link rewriting) for imported posts via a hidden second cooking path

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook now returns `raw` immediately when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, so it never executes `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. This creates a second cooking path that bypasses the existing post-cook plugin hook entirely. The diff also shows imported content being created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (TopicEmbed.import via PostCreator), so this bypass is not theoretical: imported/embed posts will skip all `:after_post_cook` plugin behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicRetriever has a TOCTOU race on duplicate import: the exists? check then import_remote allows concurrent retrieves; the unique index catches the insert but the failure relies on TopicEmbed.create! raising an unhandled exception rather than handling the race

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve, it checks `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?` and then later calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`. In `TopicEmbed.import`, it again does `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and if blank proceeds to `Topic.transaction` and `TopicEmbed.create!`. With concurrent retrievals for the same URL, both can pass the `exists?/first` checks and both attempt `create!`; the unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` will reject the second insert, raising (e.g.) `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`/`RecordInvalid`. There is no rescue/handling in `TopicRetriever`, the job, or `TopicEmbed.import`, so the race can cause an unhandled exception even though the DB constraint prevents duplicates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117 (and 140-145): Existing disqus import tool's contract silently rewritten in unrelated feature PR — deleting the :category option breaks existing scripts/automation invoking 'disqus import -c', with no migration path

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the CLI option `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` and deletes the associated logic that read `options[:category]` and passed a `category`/`category_id` into `PostCreator`. After this change, invoking `disqus import -c <category>` will error due to an unknown option, and there is no replacement/migration path shown in the diff. This is a backward-incompatible behavior change to the existing import tool.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:117 (and 140-145): Import semantics silently flipped from creating a permalink-stub topic (deterministic, no network I/O) to fetching and parsing live remote articles, causing failures/hangs on dead or moved links and raw-HTML-cooked output instead of link stubs, contradicting the PR title 'Enhance embed URL handling and validation'

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` from creating a local stub topic via `PostCreator.new(... raw: "[[Permalink](#{t[:link]})]")` to calling `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`, which (per new `TopicEmbed.import_remote`) does `open(url).read` and parses the fetched HTML with `ruby-readability`. This is a concrete semantic shift: it introduces live network I/O during import (with no explicit timeouts/error handling shown here) and the created post is imported as HTML and marked `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (see `TopicEmbed.import`), so output differs from the previous deterministic permalink-only stub. Those consequences (possible failures/hangs on unreachable links and different content/cooking behavior) are directly verifiable in the diff. The mention of PR title contradiction isn’t verifiable from the diff, but the underlying behavioral change is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:5: Adding force: true to an already-shipped historical migration makes any rollback-and-re-run destructively drop and recreate top_topics, destroying computed topic statistics, and causes upgraded and fresh installs to run different effective schema history

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In normal Rails operation, a migration that has already run will not be re-run on upgraded installs, and on fresh installs the table does not yet exist—so `force: true` has no effect. The proposed concern about “upgraded and fresh installs run different effective schema history” is not verifiable from this change. The rollback-and-re-run scenario would already drop the table on rollback (Rails `drop_table` on down), so data loss would occur regardless; `force: true` does not introduce an additional destructive behavior in that common path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:5: Editing an applied migration appears to be a patch-over of a 'table already exists' development failure without addressing the root cause

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. While `force: true` will drop/recreate the table *if the migration is executed when the table already exists*, the proposed finding’s core claim (“editing an applied migration” and that it’s a patch-over for a dev failure “without addressing root cause”) is speculative and not verifiable from the diff. Rails will not rerun an already-applied migration, so this change typically won’t affect existing environments; it mainly changes behavior only if/when the migration runs on a DB where `top_topics` already exists but the migration is not recorded. That potential risk isn’t what the finding asserts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33 + app/models/post.rb:131-134 + app/views/embed/best.html.erb:21: raw_html cook path silently deletes the 'cooked content is always sanitized' invariant — poll_feed passes unsanitized feed HTML through TopicEmbed.import to PostCreator with cook_method raw_html, which skips the sanitization pipeline, and best.html.erb renders it with raw, allowing persisted and executed HTML/JS in the forum origin and in every third-party embedding page via embed.js

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff explicitly adds a `cook_method` enum with a `:raw_html` option (app/models/post.rb) and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw` when `cook_method == raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `Jobs::PollFeed` parses a remote RSS/ATOM feed and passes `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` into `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates a post via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (skip_validations: true). That means arbitrary HTML from the feed becomes the persisted post body without sanitization. Then `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` renders it as HTML via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any injected HTML/JS in the feed content will execute in the Discourse origin when the embed iframe is loaded. This is a concrete XSS vector introduced by the new raw_html cook path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33: The ruby-readability tag whitelist used in TopicEmbed.import_remote is not exercised by PollFeed, which passes i.content straight to import with zero filtering

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. `Jobs::PollFeed` builds `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passes it directly into `TopicEmbed.import(...)` with no sanitization/whitelisting. `TopicEmbed.import` then creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `:raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. In contrast, `TopicEmbed.import_remote` runs `ruby-readability` with an explicit tags/attributes whitelist before importing. So RSS/Atom feed content can include arbitrary HTML (including potentially dangerous tags/attributes) that will be stored and rendered as-is, making the lack of filtering in `PollFeed` a verifiable security/correctness defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:20: 'Imported from' attribution link interpolates an unvalidated, attacker-controllable URL (from feed item link/id or embed_url request parameter) directly into a single-quoted href HTML attribute, enabling attribute breakout and HTML/JS injection into post bodies — contradicting the PR's stated objective of embed URL validation

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends an attribution HTML snippet built via string interpolation: `"#{url}"` and then stores it as post `raw` with `cook_method: :raw_html`, which makes `Post#cook` return `raw` unmodified (skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline) and the embed view renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. The only validation on `url` is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent attacker-controlled characters like a single quote or additional attributes (e.g., `http://x/' onmouseover='...`) from breaking out of the single-quoted `href` attribute and injecting HTML/JS into the post body. This `url` is attacker-controllable from RSS/Atom items (`i.link`/`i.id`) and potentially from the `embed_url` parameter path as well. So the finding describes a real injection risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: untrusted third-party RSS feed HTML rendered unescaped via `raw post.cooked` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:23; the raw_html cook method (post.rb:132-134) short-circuits the cooking/sanitize pipeline, so <script>, <iframe>, onerror= handlers, and javascript: hrefs from the polled feed are stored verbatim and served to every viewer of the embed and topic pages

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `raw_html` cook method that makes `Post#cook` return `raw` directly (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), bypassing Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` uses this mode when creating posts from RSS/imported content (`PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), ... cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`). The RSS polling job (`Jobs::PollFeed`) feeds in `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` without any HTML sanitization/allowlist, and `absolutize_urls` only adjusts relative URLs (does not remove `<script>`, event handlers, `javascript:` URLs, etc.). The embed view then renders the result with `raw post.cooked`, ensuring any injected HTML is emitted unescaped. This is a verifiable stored-XSS vector when the configured feed/remote content contains malicious HTML.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attribute-injection XSS in app/models/topic_embed.rb:12: user-supplied embed_url is interpolated unescaped into an HTML attribute (#{url}); validation only checks for http(s) prefix and host equality, so a URL containing a single quote or >"> payload injects arbitrary attributes/elements that become stored XSS

SSRF via redirect in TopicEmbed.import_remote + TopicRetriever: server-side open(url).read follows HTTP redirects without re-validating the host, and the DNS-rebinding gap (separate DNS resolutions between host check and connection) allows bouncing the fetch to internal addresses such as http://169.254.169.254/, cloud metadata endpoints, or internal admin panels, with fetched content persisted into public topics

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `TopicRetriever` only validates the initial `@embed_url` by comparing `URI(@embed_url).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, but the actual fetch happens later in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` via `open(url).read`. Ruby `open-uri` follows HTTP redirects by default and does not automatically enforce “same host” redirects, and this code does not re-check the final resolved URL/host after redirects. Therefore, an allowed URL on the embeddable host that issues a redirect can cause the server to fetch arbitrary HTTP(S) endpoints (including internal/metadata IPs), and the retrieved content is then imported/persisted via `TopicEmbed.import(...)`. Additionally, the host check is purely string-based (no IP allow/deny), so DNS rebinding between the check and the fetch is also a plausible bypass in this flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Trust-the-client authorization in app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26: the Referer header is the sole authorization gate and is client-controlled/trivially forged, so any anonymous user can fetch embed/best for any URL and enqueue arbitrary retrieve_topic background jobs causing the server to fetch attacker-chosen URLs; the 30s auto-reloading loading view amplifies load

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, access is granted solely by comparing `URI(request.referer || '').host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and then setting `X-Frame-Options = ALLOWALL`. The `Referer` header is client-supplied and can be trivially spoofed (e.g., curl/custom clients), so this is not a robust authorization gate. With a forged Referer and a chosen `embed_url` param, an unauthenticated caller can reach `best`, and when no embed exists it will enqueue `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)`. The background job will then cause server-side fetching via `TopicRetriever`/`TopicEmbed.import_remote(open(url)...)` as long as the URL host matches `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`; an attacker can vary paths to bypass the per-URL Redis throttle and force many fetches to the allowed host. The auto-reloading `loading` view can further multiply requests when embedded, but the core issue (trusting Referer for access control leading to abuse of job enqueue/server-side fetches) is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unsafe postMessage target in app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:10: attacker-controlled request.referer is interpolated into an inline <script> string context; currently protected only by incidental ERB HTML-escaping behavior, and any escaping change or html_safe use would enable direct script injection; posting to the full referer URL also leaks the parent page's path and query to the iframe target
matched_golden_ids: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden comment and the candidate issue identify that attacker-controlled `request.referer` is being interpolated into an inline JavaScript context without robust, context-appropriate escaping, creating a potential XSS/script injection vector. The candidate adds extra concerns (postMessage target/leakage) but still flags the same core XSS risk from `request.referer` in JS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fragile origin check in embed.js:17: discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 is a substring match rather than origin equality (indexOf(...) === 0), so a parent at https://evil-host.example.com would be accepted if discourseUrl contains it as a substring
embed.js:17 assigns e.data.height to iframe height without validating it is a number, allowing malformed style values (limited impact, no injection sink beyond the height attribute)

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/embed.js, the message handler sets `iframe.height = e.data.height + "px"` when it sees `{type: 'discourse-resize'}` but only checks `e.data.height` for truthiness, not that it’s a number. Since `postMessage` data is not inherently typed/trusted, a malformed/non-numeric `height` value would produce an invalid height attribute value (e.g., `"abcpx"`, `"100%px"`) and break resizing behavior. This is a real robustness/correctness issue present in the diff (even if impact is limited).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:36 calls i.content.scrub which raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content element, a reliability bug

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, feed items are processed with `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`. With SimpleRSS, `i.content` can be `nil` for many RSS feeds (they often provide `description`/`summary` but not `content`). Calling `.scrub` on `nil` will raise `NoMethodError`, crashing the poll job for such items. The diff does not guard against missing content, so this is a real reliability defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed#feed_key computes a cache key that is never used, so the feed is re-fetched and re-imported hourly with only the SHA1 dedupe protecting against churn

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `feed_key` is defined to memoize a Redis-style key (`"feed-modified:..."`) but it is never referenced anywhere in the job. The job’s `execute` method calls `poll_feed`, and `poll_feed` unconditionally does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items` every time it runs (scheduled hourly). The only built-in guard against repeated processing is inside `TopicEmbed.import`, which dedupes by `embed_url` and updates based on `content_sha1`, but there is no use of `feed_key` (or any other cache) to skip refetch/reparse when the feed hasn’t changed. So the finding that the cache key is unused and the feed will be refetched on each run is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guard tests in spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:16-26 for 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' pass for the wrong reason: the stubbed settings are never evaluated because Ruby's && short-circuits on the default-false feed_polling_enabled, so deleting SiteSetting.feed_polling_url.present? or SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present? from the guard would still keep tests green

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In Jobs::PollFeed#execute the guard is `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled? && SiteSetting.feed_polling_url.present? && SiteSetting.embed_by_username.present?`. In `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb`, the tests "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" only stub `feed_polling_url`/`embed_by_username` to nil but do not stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to true. Since `feed_polling_enabled` is added with default `false` in `config/site_settings.yml`, `feed_polling_enabled?` will be false and Ruby `&&` will short-circuit, so `feed_polling_url.present?` / `embed_by_username.present?` won’t be evaluated. Those tests would stay green even if the latter guard clauses were removed, so they are ineffective and pass for the wrong reason.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The entire body of poll_feed in app/jobs/poll_feed.rb:26-40 has zero test coverage; RSS parsing, Atom fallback URL fix, CGI.unescapeHTML on possibly-nil content (NoMethodError risk), and the TopicEmbed.import loop are never executed — only mock-invocation of the private method is verified

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The added spec `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only asserts that `execute` calls or does not call `poll_feed` based on SiteSetting stubs; it never exercises the actual `poll_feed` implementation (the `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`, the per-item URL fallback `url = i.id if ...`, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, or the `TopicEmbed.import` loop). Therefore the body of `poll_feed` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:26-40) has no direct test coverage in this diff, and the noted `i.content.scrub` call would indeed raise if `i.content` is nil (a realistic risk given feed variability), but it is not tested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 'valid host' tests in spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:31-43 stub retrieved_recently?, mirroring the implementation against itself; the real Redis throttle logic ($redis.setnx / $redis.expire at lib/topic_retriever.rb:24-30) and the staff no_throttle bypass in app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb:20 are never exercised

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb the “valid host” examples stub `retrieved_recently?` (lines 31-43 in the new file), so the Redis throttling code inside `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` (lib/topic_retriever.rb: the `$redis.setnx` / `$redis.expire` path) is never executed by these tests. Also, nothing in the added specs exercises the `no_throttle` bypass wired in Jobs::RetrieveTopic (`TopicRetriever.new(..., no_throttle: user.try(:staff?))`), so that behavior is untested in this diff. This is a verifiable test coverage/quality gap introduced alongside new throttle/bypass logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: perform_retrieve's real decision logic is stubbed in every test in spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, leaving the 'bail if embed already exists' check, the RSS-first branch, fetch_http fall-through, and the 'return if user.blank?' guard untested; the new app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb job (InvalidParameters raise, staff no_throttle derivation) also has no spec

adjudication.rationale: This is verifiable from the diff: in `spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb` the “valid host” examples stub `retrieved_recently?` and only assert whether `perform_retrieve` is called, but never exercise `perform_retrieve` itself. That leaves branches inside `perform_retrieve` untested (early return if `TopicEmbed.exists?`, the RSS-first `Jobs::PollFeed` path, and `fetch_http` including `return if user.blank?`). Also, the newly added job `app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb` (argument validation raising `Discourse::InvalidParameters`, and `no_throttle` based on `user.try(:staff?)`) has no corresponding spec added in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The skip-validations branch at lib/post_revisor.rb:85 is only exercised with data that passes validation anyway (spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:40-43 revises with a valid body), so the behavioral change of save(validate: false) is never verified; a test revising to content that fails validation is needed

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `PostRevisor#update_post` to `@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`, and the new embed import path (`TopicEmbed.import` update case) does call `revise!` with `skip_validations: true`. However, the proposed finding is about insufficient test coverage (no spec demonstrating behavior when validations would fail), not a concrete bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff. The branch is exercised, and lack of a negative validation test is not a verifiable problem in the code itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The update-path test in spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:40-43 never asserts that the new content_sha1 was persisted via update_column, so deleting that line would still keep the test green while causing repeated revise-branch re-entry on every feed poll

adjudication.rationale: In spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb the "Supports updating the post" example only asserts that the returned post content changes (post.cooked =~ /new contents/). It never reloads the TopicEmbed record nor asserts that embed.content_sha1 was updated. In TopicEmbed.import’s update path, preventing repeated updates relies on `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`; if that line were removed or broken, the test would still pass while the code would re-enter the revise branch on every subsequent poll because `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1` would remain true. This is a real, verifiable test coverage gap in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 'creates a topic view when a topic_id is found' test in spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:49-53 stubs TopicView.new with a mock, so only the constructor call is verified; bad 'best: 5' options, TopicView argument-contract changes, and rendering regressions against real data would go undetected

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb the example `creates a topic view when a topic_id is found` does `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})`, which verifies the constructor arguments (including `{best: 5}`) and does not stub it “with a mock” beyond setting an expectation. The finding is essentially a critique that the test is not an integration/behavior test and won’t catch rendering regressions or future contract changes—this is a general testing-depth concern, not a concrete bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_column :posts, :cook_method with DEFAULT + NOT NULL causes full table rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on PostgreSQL <11, blocking all reads/writes on posts during deploy; safe pattern (add nullable → backfill → set NOT NULL) not used

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds migration `20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb` with `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions prior to 11, adding a column with a non-null default generally rewrites the whole table and requires an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, which can block reads/writes to `posts` during deploy. The safer multi-step pattern (add nullable, backfill, then set default and NOT NULL) is not used here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embeds rows have NOT NULL topic_id/post_id but no foreign keys and no dependent: cleanup, so deleting a topic/post leaves orphaned rows that cause EmbedController#best to 500 and TopicRetriever/PollFeed to raise NoMethodError with no purge step

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `topic_embeds` table with `topic_id` and `post_id` declared `null: false` plus a unique index on `embed_url`, but it adds no foreign-key constraints and the `TopicEmbed` model has `belongs_to :topic` / `:post` with no `dependent:` cleanup on the Topic/Post side. The code then assumes these associations exist: `EmbedController#best` uses `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` (pluck) and unconditionally builds `TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)`, which will blow up if that topic was deleted. Likewise `TopicEmbed.import` does `post = embed.post` and on content changes calls `PostRevisor.new(post)`; if the post was deleted (or the association is broken), `post` is nil and this will raise. There is no purge/repair path for orphaned `topic_embeds` rows in the diff, so orphaning can cause runtime errors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_url is a varchar(255) with unique index but URLs longer than 255 chars are valid; PollFeed has no per-item rescue and retry: false, so an over-length URL raises StatementInvalid, aborts the entire feed poll run, permanently blocks all subsequent items in that feed, and data loss goes unreported

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` adds `t.string :embed_url, null: false` with a unique index. In Rails this is a varchar(255) by default, and valid URLs can exceed 255 chars. In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, each feed item calls `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, ...)` without per-item rescue; `TopicEmbed.import` will `create!` a `TopicEmbed` row using `embed_url: url`, so an over-length URL would raise (e.g., `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` / value too long) and abort the entire poll run. Since the scheduled job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, Sidekiq won’t automatically retry the failed execution, and subsequent items in that run won’t be processed; if the problematic item remains in the feed, future hourly runs will keep failing at that item unless the feed changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Already-shipped migration create_top_topics is edited to add force: true, which will silently DROP and recreate a populated top_topics table on databases where the table exists but the version row is missing (e.g., restored backup), losing all topic ranking data

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration (20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it. If this migration ever runs on an environment where `top_topics` exists but the schema_migrations entry for this version is missing/out of sync (e.g., certain restore/repair situations), it would destroy any existing `top_topics` data without warning. This data-loss risk is introduced by the change shown in the diff.
